newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slip amid lack of fresh cash.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slip amid lack of fresh cash.

text.p: Turkish shares dipped in narrow trade on Tuesday amid no fresh cash entry and as some cash flowed out of the market into alternative investment instruments ahead of a long weekend, brokers said.

"The index started easing amid lack of fresh cash inflow after it could not pierce the 65,000 (point) resistance. Players also diverted to other investments ahead of the long weekend," said Ugur Under from Boyut Securities.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC lost 0.85 percent or 547.02 points to end at 64,199.55. Daily volume dropped to 5.2 trillion lira from Monday's 7.8 trillion lira.

There was a cash shortage in the system on Tuesday when the central bank did not lend banks overnight money. The banks repaid the central bank 14.2 trillion which they borrowed through overnight dealings on Monday.
Brokers said trade was likely to remain squeezed in a tight band between 63,500 and 65,000 in the next few days if the lack of fresh cash inflow continued.
But the market was unlikely to break strong support at 63,500, they added.
Many players preferred to tie their cash to six-day repos where the yields were attractive ahead of a long weekend which will start from Friday, a national holiday, brokers said.
The average rate on the six-day repo was 73 percent.
They said the results of today's 189-day t-bill auction where the Treasury sold 36.16 trillion lira worth bills at an average yield of 135.0 percent had no impact on the market.
The session's most active shares were those of Turkish Airlines which stayed steady at 26,500 lira. Shares of Isbank also were unchanged at 9,000 lira.
The 85-share industrial index .ISEI lost 0.68 percent to 70,767.21 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF also dived by 1.29 percent to 55,911.97.
Of the 217 shares traded, losers surpassed gainers by 131 to 31 and 55 shares were stable.
